findings.reason: the §1 premise is factually wrong and §3 must cite and reuse this reproduction rather than re-derive it as if nothing survived.
findings.text: §1 states "No evaluation code survived. Every AUC was a one-off stdin script", but the exact figure the plan adopts as §3's positive control — the source-label AUC 0.9244 [0.8858, 0.9608] over `docs/evidence/fragments/discovery-judgments-through-jev/labelled-path-categories.json` with `canonical_copy` units — is already asserted at tests/discovery/test_path_category_gate.py:122-146 (`assert auc == pytest.approx(0.9244, abs=0.0001)`). The plan also mis-states §3's fixture path: it says `labelled-path-categories.json`, the file lives under `docs/evidence/fragments/discovery-judgments-through-jev/`, and its rows are already loaded and grouped by `canonical_copy` in that test.

findings.reason: §3 should state why a re-implementation is preferred to `sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score`/`accuracy_score`/`f1_score`/`confusion_matrix`, or call them.
findings.text: `scikit-learn>=1.7.2` is a declared dependency and `roc_auc_score` is already imported and used at tests/discovery/test_path_category_gate.py:142 to compute the plan's own positive control, yet §3 proposes a hand-rolled rank-based `paired_auc` and does not cite the library anywhere in §3. Rank AUC, accuracy, macro-F1 and the confusion table are all `sklearn.metrics` calls.

findings.reason: §3 should name the owners it will extend or fold, or justify a third location for metrics that already have two homes.
findings.text: census of the existing evaluation owners §3 duplicates without naming: `imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark_roles.py:1201 discrimination_metrics` (rank AUC computed at :1231, "auc — probability a random good outranks a random bad"), `:113 RoleBenchReport` with `:108 cost_per_item` (the report+per-item-cost owner §3's `cost_latency_summary` reproduces), `:205 verdict_flip_quality` (the flip-rate metric §3's `option_order_stability` reproduces), `:1108 load_discrimination_corpus` and `:1170 build_advisory_paired_corpus` (the labelled-corpus loaders §3's `load_labelled_fixture` reproduces), `:170 spearman_rho`; and on the SN benchmark side `imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark.py:64 ReviewerScores`, `:81 ModelResult`, `:216 BenchmarkReport`, `:2063 _render_reviewer_agreement` with `:2118 _spearman_rho` (the reviewer-agreement owner §5's Cohen's-kappa reading should sit beside). §3 instead places a single shared copy under `imas_codex/discovery/base/evaluation.py` and asserts it is "one copy" while leaving these two SN-side owners unmentioned.

findings.reason: §3 must justify the wrappers or drop them in favour of the library and the existing metric owners.
findings.text: `paired_auc`, `bootstrap_interval` and `classification_metrics` are thin wrappers over `scikit-learn` metrics and a resample loop; §3 does not say why the library cannot be extended/used or why the existing metric owners cannot absorb them, so the new module adds public surface (`public_definitions` 0 → 8) without adding depth for three of its eight functions. `choose_operating_point` and `frozen_state_variation` are the two with real content.

findings.reason: each adding section must account for the interface surface it adds, which is the item's binding rule.
findings.text: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a `[tool.imas-codex.sn-judge]` seat (the repo already carries ~20 `[tool.imas-codex.*]` seats that resolve through `get_model`, pyproject.toml:432,453), §3 adds a new module of eight public functions, and §6 adds schema fields plus regenerated models (imas_codex/graph/models.py) — none of the three sections states in its own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be. §3 in particular is adding metric surface beside two existing metric owners and names neither.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §3's one module hides fixture loading, paired AUC, the bootstrap, operating-point choice and the stability checks behind eight functions, and §2/§6 extend their named owners (`decide_batch`, `_build_review_record`) rather than forking them.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-implements evaluation that `imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark_roles.py` and `imas_codex/standard_names/benchmark.py` already own, and does not name either.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a `[tool.imas-codex.sn-judge]` seat, §3 a module of eight public functions, §6 schema fields and generated models, and none of the three sections names what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan asserts "No evaluation code survived; every AUC was a one-off stdin script" (§1) and proposes new evaluation machinery (§3), but the source-label AUC it names as its positive control is already computed in-tree, and scripted metrics owners already exist.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — several §3 functions are thin re-encodings of `scikit-learn`, a declared dependency already in use, and §3 does not say why the library cannot be used or the existing metrics owners extended.
